bindingId.description: Identifies one exact issued runtime binding instance (D-022). It is a reference to execution authority, never proof of authorization by itself. It must not silently retarget to another action, action version, runtime target, or authority context; a materially changed target requires a newly issued binding ID, and old IDs are never reused for replacement targets. Unknown binding IDs fail closed.

action.description: The exact Action Definition this binding executes, identified by id plus exact version. Runtime execution requires that exact id+version to be registered and available; bindings do not float across versions.

id.description: Action Definition identifier. `ActionReference.id` uses the canonical Action ID grammar defined by the Action Definition contract; it is not a separate identifier namespace. Must reference a registered Action Definition.

version.description: Exact Action Definition version this binding is valid for.

driver.description: Extensible driver identifier (D-016), not a closed enum: frameworks (e.g. livewire, htmx, liveview, http) and namespaced custom drivers are all expressed here as plain identifiers. A runtime may execute a binding only if this driver is explicitly registered/supported; unknown drivers fail closed; no fallback to another driver is permitted.

lifecycle.description: Which runtime authority the binding's validity is tied to (D-023). `page`: one runtime-defined page/surface instance, not necessarily a browser document; when that instance ends the binding becomes stale. `component`: one specific component instance; rerenders of the same instance do not necessarily invalidate it, and a replacement instance never inherits the binding merely by sharing class, method name, DOM position, or business record. `session`: a trusted runtime session authority resolved from trusted state, never ordinary caller input; expires, is revoked, logs out, or rotates in a way that invalidates prior bindings makes it stale. `persistent`: not intrinsically tied to page/component/session lifetime, but never permanent, global, or anonymous: it remains subject to explicit revocation, expiresAt, exact action version availability, driver availability, and all other runtime policy.

target.description: Driver-owned execution target data. Its shape is owned by the named driver; the core contract does not enumerate driver target shapes. Binding details belong here or in driver code, never in the Action Definition.

expiresAt.description: Independent hard upper time bound on binding validity (D-024). Lifecycle and expiry are cumulative, not alternatives; whichever invalidates first wins. null or absence means no explicit contract-level time deadline and does not disable lifecycle invalidation or revocation. Expired bindings fail closed. Compare deterministically, UTC-oriented.

extensions.description: Namespaced extension point for adapter/driver metadata. Keys must be of the form `namespace/key`. Extensions never alter identity, lifecycle, or expiry semantics.
